stories.title: Bitcoin's $85,000 Sell Wall Disappears as Traders Eye $100,000
stories.summary: A large sell order at $85,000 has vanished from Bitcoin's order book, and traders are now positioning for a move toward $100,000. Separately, a reported $88 billion drop in bank reserves is raising liquidity-squeeze concerns, though analysts say it does not yet prove one. Bitcoin has also held up through a period of 5% yields, but commentators argue crypto's broader cheap-money era is ending.
stories.whyItMatters: These three signals together show a market testing new highs just as the macro backdrop for cheap liquidity shifts.
whatToWatch: Whether price action confirms a push toward $100,000
Further data on bank reserve levels and liquidity conditions
How crypto markets adjust to a higher-yield environment
questions: Is the $100,000 bet based on real demand or thin order books?
Does the bank reserve drop actually tighten crypto liquidity?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s $85,000 sell wall is gone and traders are now betting on $100,000
Why an $88 billion bank reserve drop doesn’t prove a Bitcoin liquidity squeeze – yet
Bitcoin survived 5% yields but crypto’s cheap-money era did not

stories.title: Hackers Exploit Third-Party Aave Tool to Steal 114 ETH
stories.summary: Attackers exploited a third-party tool connected to the Aave lending protocol and stole 114 ETH. The core Aave protocol itself was not reported as compromised; the breach points to a tool built on top of it.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows that DeFi users remain exposed to risk through third-party integrations, even when the underlying protocol holds up.
whatToWatch: Any response or patch from the tool's developers
Whether Aave issues its own statement or guidance
Reports on recovery of the stolen funds
questions: Which third-party tool was exploited, and how?
Can the stolen ETH be recovered or frozen?

sources.title: Crypto hackers exploit third-party Aave tool to steal 114 ETH

stories.title: Bitcoin Rallies Overnight as ETF Demand Returns Ahead of Jobs Report
stories.summary: Bitcoin posted a sharp overnight rally, with reports pointing to renewed ETF demand. The move comes just before a closely watched US jobs report that could shape near-term Fed rate expectations.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key gauge of institutional demand, and the jobs report could swing the rate outlook that drives crypto risk appetite.
whatToWatch: Whether ETF inflows continue in the following days
questions: How large were the actual ETF inflows behind this rally?
Will the rally hold once jobs data lands?

sources.title: Bitcoin sees big overnight rally as ETF demand returns before the next US jobs test

stories.title: Unpatched Eclair Lightning Nodes Risk Repeated Crashes on Restart
stories.summary: A flaw in the Eclair Lightning Network implementation can cause unpatched Bitcoin nodes to crash again each time they restart. Node operators running Eclair without the fix remain exposed.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning Network reliability underpins Bitcoin's main payment-layer use case, so a recurring crash bug threatens that infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Whether the flaw is exploited in the wild before nodes update
questions: How many Eclair nodes remain unpatched?
Has the bug already caused outages for users?

sources.title: Unpatched Eclair Bitcoin Lightning nodes could crash again every time they restart

stories.title: Cardano's DeFi Activity Has Shrunk by More Than Half as RealFi Bets on Credit
stories.summary: Activity in Cardano's DeFi ecosystem has fallen by more than half. A newer effort called RealFi is betting that real-world credit products can bring capital and users back.
stories.whyItMatters: The outcome will test whether real-world-asset lending can revive activity on a smaller layer-1 chain that has lost DeFi momentum.
whatToWatch: RealFi's rollout and early adoption numbers
Whether Cardano DeFi metrics stabilize or keep declining
questions: What drove the more-than-50% decline in the first place?
Can credit products attract capital that other DeFi apps could not?

sources.title: Cardano’s DeFi has shrunk by more than half and RealFi is betting credit can revive it

stories.title: Evernorth's Nasdaq XRP Treasury Approved, but Buying Power Falls Short of $300 Million
stories.summary: Evernorth's XRP treasury vehicle has won approval for a Nasdaq listing. Its actual buying power, however, is reportedly less than the $300 million figure that had been expected.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors watch XRP treasury vehicles as a proxy for institutional demand, so the gap between the expected and real funding matters more than the approval itself.
whatToWatch: Clarified figures on its actual available capital
questions: Why is the real buying power lower than the $300 million expected?
What is the confirmed funding figure?

stories.title: Strategy's STRC Calculator Shows $210 for a Share Redeemable at $101
stories.summary: Strategy's published calculator values its STRC shares at $210, but the company can redeem those same shares at $101. The gap has drawn scrutiny over what the calculator actually represents.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors relying on the calculator's figure for a Bitcoin-linked instrument need to know it does not match the redemption price.
whatToWatch: Any clarification or correction from Strategy
Investor and analyst reaction to the discrepancy
questions: Why do the calculator value and redemption price differ so much?
Is the calculator's methodology flawed or just misleading?

sources.title: Why Strategy’s STRC calculator shows $210 for a share it can redeem at $101

stories.title: US Targets $17 Billion Russia-Linked Crypto Payment Network Built on USDT
stories.summary: US authorities have taken action against a crypto payment network valued at $17 billion that is allegedly linked to Russia. The network reportedly used Tether's USDT stablecoin as a route around sanctions.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows regulators are increasingly focused on stablecoins as a channel for sanctions evasion, which could bring more scrutiny to USDT.
whatToWatch: Further US Treasury or enforcement actions against the network
questions: How will the action actually be enforced against the network?
Does this affect USDT's broader liquidity or usage?

sources.title: US targets $17 billion Russia-linked crypto payment network using USDT as an escape route
